chunks: Zur‘ah ibn Muḥammad al-Ḥaḍramī narrated from Samā‘ah ibn Mihrān, who said: I heard him say:

Indeed Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has promised two punishments for consuming the wealth of the orphan. As for one of them, it is the punishment of the Hereafter by the Fire; and as for the punishment of this world, it is His statement, Mighty and Majestic:
Let those fear who, if they left behind weak offspring, would fear for them; so let them be wary of Allah and speak a right word.
This means: let him fear that He may treat his offspring after him as he dealt with these orphans.

key_terms.الْآخِرَةِ: the Hereafter, the final abode after death
key_terms.بِالنَّارِ: with the Fire, meaning punishment in Hell
key_terms.ذُرِّيَّةً ضِعَافاً: weak offspring in need of protection
key_terms.عُقُوبَتَيْنِ: two punishments, one worldly and one in the Hereafter
key_terms.مَالِ الْيَتِيمِ: the property or wealth belonging to an orphan

ai.seo_question: What punishment is mentioned for consuming an orphan’s wealth in this world and the Hereafter?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that consuming the wealth of an orphan brings two punishments: one in the Hereafter through the Fire, and one in this world through a corresponding harm affecting one’s own descendants. It cites the Quranic verse to warn people to consider how they would fear for their own weak children and thus act justly toward orphans.
